name: Pennsylvania
overview: Pennsylvania sells the delinquent property itself rather than a lien. In most counties the county Tax Claim Bureau runs the sales under the Real Estate Tax Sale Law. The annual upset sale must be scheduled no earlier than the second Monday of September and before October 1, and many counties hold a continued upset sale and a judicial sale in December. A judicial sale offers the property freed of liens, and property still unsold goes to a repository for private bids. The law allows no redemption after the actual sale, so owners must pay before it. Philadelphia instead sells tax-delinquent property through Sheriff's sales held online on Bid4Assets.

counties.how_to_bid: Both live auctions run online on Bid4Assets. Register with Bid4Assets, complete vesting and funding, e-sign the bidder affidavit and upload ID and entity documents, then book a virtual or in-person meeting with the Tax Claim Bureau through the link Bid4Assets sends, and fund your deposit (amount not stated on the county page). counties.how_to_bid: Upset and judicial sales are online through GovEase and require pre-registration in the posted window (judicial bidders upload documents to GovEase; in-person registration is not accepted).
